meta.rounding: floats rounded to 3 decimals; attention rows renormalized after rounding

sentences.label: A pronoun finds its noun
sentences.note: Watch who 'she' listens to. In the middle layers, heads link the pronoun back to 'nurse' — the model resolves reference with attention weights, not grammar rules.
sentences.text: The nurse told the patient that she would return soon

sentences.label: A phrase repeats
sentences.note: When the phrase starts over, induction-style heads in the middle layers point the last 'clock' back at the first one — and at what followed it.
sentences.text: the clock ticked, the clock ticked, the clock

sentences.label: Two people, one boat
sentences.note: Names, a possession, and a transfer. Attention has to keep Maria, Diego, and the boat in separate lanes while the sentence moves them around.
sentences.text: Maria sold her old boat to Diego last spring

sentences.label: A fact it knows
sentences.note: Ten tokens in, the model puts almost all of its probability on one surname. The logit lens below shows that answer assembling layers before the output — and competing names dying off as it does.
sentences.text: The first man to walk on the moon was Neil

sentences.label: Agreement across a gap
sentences.note: 'Keys' is plural, 'cabinet' is singular and much closer to the verb. The model still lands on 'are' — number has to survive the distance.
sentences.text: The keys to the cabinet are on the table

sentences.label: Offshore, briefly
sentences.note: A lighter one. Even a toy sentence gets the full treatment: twelve layers of second-guessing before the next word.
sentences.text: The robot checked the compass and sailed on

sentences.label: They, and it
sentences.note: Two pronouns, two different anchors: 'they' reaches back to the engineers, 'it' to the bridge. Same mechanism, different targets.
sentences.text: When the engineers finished the bridge, they opened it to traffic
